summary: This feature spotlights local female-led sports teams and leagues, including a running club, a women's football league, boxing, a triathlon series, youth soccer, and a basketball league. It profiles the founders and athletes behind them and their goals of inclusivity, empowerment, and breaking stereotypes. It closes with the need for sustained community support and funding, noting initiatives like Girls' Sports Day.
one_line: A profile of local female-led sports teams and leagues, their founders, and their push for inclusion, empowerment, and sustained community support.
key_facts: The 'Sprint Queens' is an all-female local running club established on September 5, 2023, by marathon runner Emily Torres.
Sarah Zimmer, a former college football stand-out, leads a local women's football league that kicked off its first season on September 15.
Jasmine Clark is a local lightweight boxer who says, "I fight to show that we, women, are powerful beyond measure, in and out of the ring."
The first women's boxing tournament is scheduled for late September, and Tuesday night fights feature local female boxers.
Amelia Hanover, marathon runner and triathlete, pioneered the 'Tri-For-Her' triathlon series, whose first race is on October 20, 2023.
The Tri-For-Her series caters to various age groups and skill levels and offers specialized training clinics for women.
Lauren Pike, a former professional soccer player turned coach, established youth soccer clinics that provide girls with training and mentorship.
On September 25, Lauren Pike's under-16 team, the 'Fury FC', won a regional tournament.
The local women's basketball league, founded by former college basketball athlete Jessica Hyde, has its finals set for November 1.
Local businesses support the women's basketball league by sponsoring teams and providing venues for games.
'Girls' Sports Day', established on September 30, promotes the health, empowerment, and academic benefits of sports participation.
City council member Claire Jordan advocates for women's sports and says, "It's crucial we keep these programs funded and accessible to all."
